never_write.region: Interrupt vector table with BSL signatures and JTAG lock signature
never_write.why: The vector table is the BSL password. A JTAG lock signature at 0xFF80 locks JTAG on FR2xx/FR4xx; recovery needs the JMB user-code erase (see recovery). On FR5xx/FR6xx a JTAG password uses the same vectors.

never_write.range: 0x1000 to 0x17FF on the FR2433 and FR5994 rows of devices.csv (BSLStart/BSLEnd)
never_write.why: TI BSL code, not for the user.
Holds user and calibration data on some parts; FR2xx/FR4xx BSL mass erase clears it. Back up before any erase.

recovery.symptom: FR5xx/FR6xx locked with a JTAG password
recovery.fix: Unlock through the JTAG mailbox: request 0x1E1E, then send the password words within 1.2 s (else the device does a BOR).

recovery.symptom: FR2xx/FR4xx locked by the JTAG lock signature at 0xFF80
recovery.fix: Hold RST, start JTAG, send mailbox 0xA55A then user-code erase 0x1A1A, release, then regain JTAG with a sync and POR.
Send a wrong password: mass erase runs, then the password is 0xFF for all bytes; works unless the mass-erase protection signatures are set.
